meta.title: Postpartum Diet & Recovery Knowledge Base - C-Section (Indian Context)
meta.scope: Uncomplicated Cesarean section recovery in an Indian mother, with or without lactation. Complications (PPH, infection, GDM, pre-eclampsia) require individualised medical care that overrides this KB.
meta.disclaimer: Educational only. Does not replace the treating obstetrician, physician or registered dietitian. Emergency in India: 108 ambulance. Mental health: Tele-MANAS 14416, Kiran 1800-599-0019.

energy.practicalTargetKcal: 2100-2300 kcal/day for a typical 55-60 kg breastfeeding mother; 1900-2100 if not breastfeeding
notes: ICMR-NIN 2020: +330 kcal/day for lactation months 0-6 (+400 for months 6-12); CDC concurs at +330-400 kcal [R1][R13]
Pregnancy fat stores fund part of milk energy cost - hence the modest increment
Postpartum weight retention is a cardiometabolic risk: safe loss 0.25-0.5 kg/week once feeding established; do not go below ~1800 kcal/day while breastfeeding [R13]
One gond laddoo = 150-250 kcal: the practical difference between recovery and weight retention

macronutrients.name: Protein
macronutrients.dailyTarget: 70-90 g/day (1.2-1.5 g/kg) during wound healing + lactation; ICMR-NIN 2020 lactation RDA ~65 g
whyItMatters: Collagen synthesis (glycine, proline, lysine) for the layered uterine and abdominal wound
Rebuilding red cells after 800-1000 mL surgical blood loss; immune function; uterine involution
Milk protein secretion ~7-8 g/day; deficiency measurably delays wound healing [R8]
sources: Vegetarian: dal/rajma/chhole 1 katori = 6-7 g; paneer 100 g = 18 g; curd 1 katori = 5 g; milk 1 glass = 6-7 g; soy chunks 25 g dry = 13 g; besan chilla 2 = 13 g; nuts 30 g = 6-7 g
Non-veg: egg 1 = 6-7 g; chicken 100 g cooked = 25 g; fish 100 g = 20 g
Cereal+pulse combining (dal-rice, khichdi, dal-roti, idli-sambar) completes amino acid profiles
practicalTips: 20-25 g protein at each of 3 meals + 10-15 g per snack
Example vegetarian day reaches ~73 g: chilla+curd (18), almonds (6), roti+dal+paneer+chaas (24), roasted chana+milk (13), dal-rice+veg (12)

macronutrients.name: Fats
macronutrients.dailyTarget: 20-30% of energy; visible fat 20-30 g/day (4-6 tsp total); DHA 200-300 mg/day
whyItMatters: Breast-milk DHA rises directly with maternal intake - supports infant brain and retina [R9]
Ghee contains no calcium, protein, vitamin C or zinc: zero bone/wound-healing properties; excess adds weight retention and LDL [see Myth #2]
Trans fats (vanaspati, packaged bakery, some namkeen) impair lipid profiles and wound microcirculation
sources: DHA: bangda (mackerel), sardines, hilsa; algae-oil supplement for vegetarians (flax/chia/walnut ALA converts at only ~5-10%)
Rotate mustard, groundnut, rice-bran oils; ghee 1-2 tsp/day as taste fat
Nuts and seeds 30 g/day: almonds, walnuts, til, flaxseed, pumpkin seeds
practicalTips: Avoid shark, swordfish; limit surmai and tuna (methylmercury) [R15]
Deep-fried items occasional, not daily, during recovery

macronutrients.name: Carbohydrates & fibre
macronutrients.dailyTarget: 45-60% of energy as complex carbohydrates; fibre 30 g+ (ICMR-NIN suggests ~40 g/2000 kcal)
whyItMatters: Fibre is the primary defence against post-op constipation (opioids, iron supplements, low mobility, surgical ileus)
Post-meal glucose spikes impair neutrophil/macrophage function - the real 'pus prevention' is balanced meals, not banning dal or rice
Ragi ~344 mg calcium/100 g - among the highest-calcium plant foods in the Indian diet [R3]
sources: Whole wheat phulka, dalia, oats, ragi, jowar, bajra, brown rice, pulses, vegetables, whole fruits
Isabgol (psyllium) 1-2 tsp at night if stool is hard - safe, evidence-based, food-grade
practicalTips: Added sugar <20-25 g/day; skip sugary 'recovery drinks'
Maida-only or white-rice-only phases prolong constipation

micronutrients.name: Iron
micronutrients.dailyTarget: ~21-23 mg/day from food (ICMR-NIN lactation RDA) + supplement as prescribed
whyItMatters: Replaces 800-1000 mL surgical blood loss; collagen synthesis is iron-dependent
>52% of Indian pregnant women are already anaemic at delivery (NFHS-5) [R12]
foodSources: dal, rajma, soy, til, chana, methi/chaulai, dates+ jaggery (small)
absorptionTips: Pair plant iron with vitamin C at the same meal (lemon on dal; guava/amla alongside) - can double absorption
Keep chai/coffee 1-2 h away from iron meals: tannins can cut absorption by a third to more than half
Never take calcium and iron tablets together
micronutrients.supplementNote: Continue prescribed iron-folic acid: WHO advises 6-12 weeks postpartum supplementation where anaemia is common [R5]

micronutrients.name: Calcium
whyItMatters: Milk draws ~250-300 mg calcium/day; low intake mobilises maternal bone
Bone mineral is recovered after weaning provided calcium+vitamin D adequacy
foodSources: ragi (344 mg/100 g), milk, curd, paneer, til/sesame, calcium-set tofu, small fish with bones [R3]
absorptionTips: Split across meals - the gut absorbs under ~500 mg at a time efficiently
Take calcium tablet at a different meal from iron
micronutrients.supplementNote: Commonly prescribed postpartum in India (e.g., 500 mg with dinner) - as per doctor

micronutrients.name: Vitamin C
whyItMatters: Collagen cross-linking enzymes (prolyl/lysyl hydroxylase) are vitamin-C dependent - scurvy classically reopens healed wounds
Doubles non-haem iron absorption when eaten with plant iron
foodSources: amla (~600 mg/100 g), guava (~200+ mg/100 g), capsicum, citrus, papaya, tomato [R3]
absorptionTips: Eat some raw or lightly cooked - prolonged boiling degrades vitamin C
One guava or amla with lunch and dinner covers the target

micronutrients.name: Vitamin D
whyItMatters: Enables calcium absorption; supports immune function
Deficiency is very common in Indian women (often 40-80% by region) and linked to body pain, cramps and low mood
foodSources: Sunlight 15-30 min on arms/face mid-morning; fortified milk; eggs; fatty fish
absorptionTips: Ask for a 25-OH-D level if fatigued or aching
micronutrients.supplementNote: Correction (commonly 60,000 IU/week x 6-8 weeks in India) is effective and cheap but must be doctor-directed

micronutrients.name: Vitamin B12
whyItMatters: The breastfed infant's B12 status depends entirely on the mother; deficiency harms infant development and blood formation
Indian vegetarian mothers are at high risk
foodSources: Milk, curd, paneer, eggs, fish, chicken
micronutrients.supplementNote: Vegetarians/vegans should supplement as per doctor

micronutrients.name: Folate
whyItMatters: Red cell production after blood loss; DNA repair during rapid tissue regeneration; future pregnancy readiness
foodSources: Green leafy vegetables, dal, rajma, besan, peanuts, wheat germ
absorptionTips: Boiling leaches folate - prefer steaming or stir-cooking greens
micronutrients.supplementNote: Part of prescribed IFA; 400 micrograms/day pre-conception if planning another pregnancy

micronutrients.name: Zinc
whyItMatters: Wound epithelialisation, collagen maturation, immune competence, taste/appetite
foodSources: Whole grains, dal, pumpkin seeds, cashew, paneer, chicken, eggs
absorptionTips: Phytates in unleavened roti limit absorption - fermentation (idli/dosa/curd) and sprouting help

micronutrients.name: Omega-3 DHA
whyItMatters: Infant brain and retinal development via breast milk; maternal inflammation resolution and mood
foodSources: bangda (Indian mackerel), sardines, hilsa; rohu/katla leaner; flax/chia/walnut provide ALA with poor conversion (~5-10%)
absorptionTips: Avoid shark and swordfish; limit surmai and tuna - methylmercury [R15]
micronutrients.supplementNote: Algae-oil DHA 200-300 mg/day is the reliable vegetarian source

micronutrients.name: Iodine
whyItMatters: Maternal thyroid function and infant neurodevelopment
foodSources: Iodised salt (check the packet), dairy, eggs
micronutrients.supplementNote: Use iodised salt for the family pot - the practical Indian solution

micronutrients.name: Vitamin A
whyItMatters: Epithelial repair of wound and uterine lining; infant stores via milk
foodSources: Papaya, mango, carrot, pumpkin, sweet potato, methi/palak, milk, egg yolk
absorptionTips: Orange vegetables + one green daily easily meet it
micronutrients.supplementNote: Food-first; avoid excess liver/preformed retinol supplements

micronutrients.name: Choline
whyItMatters: Depleted rapidly in lactation; infant brain development
foodSources: Egg yolk (~140 mg/egg - richest common source), milk, soy, groundnut, whole grains
absorptionTips: One egg a day is the cheapest choline strategy
micronutrients.supplementNote: Strict vegetarians: cover with soy/milk volumes or as advised

micronutrients.name: Magnesium & selenium
micronutrients.dailyTarget: Via mixed diet (nuts, whole grains, seeds)
whyItMatters: Cramp prevention, thyroid function, antioxidant defence
foodSources: Nuts 30 g/day, whole grains, dal, seeds; 1-2 Brazil nuts cover selenium

hydration.dailyTargetMl: 2500-3000 ml total fluids/day while breastfeeding (counting milk, chaas, dal, soup, coconut water)
countAsFluids: water (boiled and cooled if supply is questionable)
notes: Breast milk is 87% water with output 750-800 ml/day; let-down thirst is a normal oxytocin signal - keep water at every feed
Drink to thirst, verify pale-straw urine; forced over-hydration does not increase milk volume, under-hydration worsens constipation and UTI [R14]
Caffeine cap 200 mg/day (1-2 cups chai/coffee), kept 1-2 h away from iron meals; no alcohol while breastfeeding [R13]

timeline.label: Days 1-3: Immediate Post-Op
timeline.theme: Clear the anaesthesia, restart the gut, begin collagen delivery, get lactation started
scienceNotes: ERAS protocols recommend early oral intake after cesarean; pooled RCT data (~1900 patients) show early feeding speeds bowel recovery without added complications [R6][R7]
Spinal anaesthesia and opioids slow the bowel; gas collects causing abdominal and shoulder-tip discomfort
Lactogenesis II arrives 30-72 h postpartum, on average ~1 day later after cesarean [R4]
Collagen synthesis begins within 24-72 h - amino acids must be delivered, not delayed
eat: Step 1 (within hours, once awake/permitted): water sips, coconut water, rice water, clear moong-dal water, clear soup
Gum chewing: sugar-free 15 min x 3-4/day until first flatus (meta-analyses shorten time to gas/stool) [R6]
Step 2 (same day/next morning): milk, thin lassi, thick dal soup, weak tea with milk
Step 3 (once passing gas, day 1-2): khichdi with 1 tsp ghee, dalia, curd-rice, upma, soft scrambled egg
Step 4 (day 2-3): soft phulka + dal + lauki sabzi, paneer bhurji, steamed fish/chicken, ripe banana/papaya
Protein at every step; 6-8 small servings daily

mealPattern.suggestion: Small serving from the current diet step; warm fluids; fluids within reach

limit: weak tea to 1 small cup, away from iron
traditionsDecoded: 'Only liquids for 3-4 days' - outdated and harmful (delays bowel recovery and protein delivery) [R7]
'First meal must be ghee halwa to push gas out' - no mechanism; adds nausea only
'No water day 1' - dangerous: constipation, UTI, poor milk
redFlags: No flatus by day 3, or distending painful abdomen with vomiting
Bleeding soaking a pad in an hour or egg-size clots
Baby feeding poorly or <6 wet diapers/day by day 5

timeline.label: Days 4-7: Early Healing (first week home)
timeline.theme: Collagen is deposited now; establish milk supply; prevent constipation; digest gently
goals: Protein + vitamin C + zinc at peak wound demand (proliferative phase days 3-21)
scienceNotes: Fibroblasts lay collagen at maximum rate days 3-21 - protein, vitamin C, zinc, iron requirements peak for tissue repair [R8]
Milk supply is governed by demand-and-supply (prolactin/oxytocin), not by special foods [R10]
eat: Early morning: warm water; 4-6 soaked almonds + 1-2 walnuts
Breakfast: methi/paneer paratha (1 tsp ghee) + curd; moong chilla; oats/dalia upma + milk; or eggs + toast
Lunch: 2 phulkas or rice + dal + any seasonal sabzi + curd/chaas + salad
Evening: roasted makhana or chana + fruit; poha with peanuts
Dinner: khichdi or dal-rice + sabzi + paneer/egg/fish/chicken (soft)

mealPattern.suggestion: Protein anchor at every eating occasion; fruit at least twice a day

traditionsDecoded: One small gond laddoo or 2-3 tbsp panjiri/day is reasonable (nuts + prebiotic gum) - a tin-full is not (each laddoo ~150-250 kcal)
Ajwain water: safe pleasant carminative - a choice, not a prescription
Methi in food amounts: modest galactagogue evidence, safe [R10]
redFlags: Painful red breast segment with fever

timeline.label: Days 8-30: The First Month (sustainable nutrient density)
timeline.theme: Full balanced Indian diet for tissue repair, milk supply and maternal stores
goals: Run the iron protocol (IFA + vitamin C pairing + tea spacing)
Full vegetable variety including traditionally banned ones
scienceNotes: ICMR My Plate for ~2000 kcal: ~270 g cereals, 85 g pulses, 300 g milk products, 350 g vegetables, 150 g fruit, 30 g nuts/seeds, ~25 g visible fat [R2]
WHO: continue iron-folic acid 6-12 weeks postpartum where anaemia is common [R5]
Confinement reframed: rest WITH movement and sunlight (immobility raises clot risk and depletes vitamin D)
eat: Healing plate rule: half vegetables + fruit, quarter protein, quarter whole grain, dairy on the side, 1-2 tsp cooking fat
All vegetables (aloo, gobi, baingan included), cooked to comfort
2 dairy servings + ragi or til preparations
Fish 2-3x/week or algae DHA if vegetarian

mealPattern.suggestion: Structure of Phase 2 with larger variety and portions to full appetite

traditionsDecoded: 'Curd is cold, avoid' - curd is protective: probiotics help gut flora recover after the surgical antibiotic course [R20]
'No grains till chhathi' - already collapsed; end any remaining ban (Myth #5)
redFlags: Persistent low mood/tearfulness/anxiety beyond 2 weeks (screen for PPD - Tele-MANAS 14416)
